name: check3-eval25-ctl
hypothesis: the collapse is unrelated to eval frequency: it reproduces at eval-every 25 (pod pid 1446666, card 3)
result: curve 432/500 (86.4%) at step 25, then 0/500 at 50/75/100; after-arm GSM8K 0/500, MMLU 69.9% (before 75.1%); length trajectory identical to the eval-every-5 control (step 32 mean 336.8, step 33 18.4, step 34 0.0)
finding: eval-every 25 vs 5 changes nothing: rollout trajectory bit-identical to the control run across all 100 steps (40/40 rows diffed steps 1-5, per-step mean lengths match to 0.1, eval-before.jsonl byte-identical). Eval frequency is exonerated as the collapse cause; the collapse is driven by the training trajectory itself.
decision: Stop treating eval frequency as a confound in the collapse attribution. Same-seed same-sha runs stay bit-comparable across trees; the live difference is the sha gap (bd72288 to 2b55eb6, diverging at step 3) plus the advantage-mask absorbing state. Next: A/B before-arm experiment, then decode on/off.
